messages.content: What does talkative mean?

Talkative means liking to talk a lot. It is an adjective.
Example: My talkative little sister told the shopkeeper all about her new school.
avalanche - what does it mean?

An avalanche is a large mass of snow and ice that slides quickly down a mountain. It is a noun.
Example: The road was closed after an avalanche covered it.
Is a doorway the same as a door? What does doorway mean?

A doorway is the opening where a door is, or the space around it. It is a noun.
Example: The cat sat in the doorway and watched the rain.
formidable? I don't know this word.

Formidable means causing fear or respect because of great strength, size or difficulty. It is an adjective.
Example: The chess champion was a formidable opponent.
Can you tell me what buckets are? I only know the singular.

Buckets are open round containers with a handle, used for carrying water or other things. It is a noun, the plural of bucket.
Example: The children carried buckets of water to the new mango saplings.
The word crunched showed up in our poem about autumn. What action is it?

Crunched means made a loud, cracking sound by being stepped on or chewed. It is a verb, the past tense of crunch.
Example: Dry leaves crunched under Lina's feet as she walked to school.
Could you define landscape? I need it for an art class.

A landscape is everything you can see when you look across an area of land, such as hills, fields and trees. It is a noun. It is also a kind of painting that shows such a view.
Example: From the hilltop, the whole landscape looked green after the rains.
A teacher wrote 'sullenness' on my brother's report. Should we worry?

Sullenness is a gloomy, silent bad mood in which a person refuses to be friendly. It is a noun. It names a mood and does not say why he feels that way.
Example: His sullenness at the table showed he was still upset about the match.
Say preparations to me like you would to a ten-year-old.

Preparations are the things you do to get ready for something. It is a noun, the plural of preparation.
Example: Everyone helped with the preparations for Diwali, from cleaning the house to making sweets.
What is anatomy? Our science teacher said we start it next term.

Anatomy is the study of the parts of a body and how they are arranged, in people, animals or plants. It is a noun.
Example: In anatomy class, Divya learned the names of the bones in the hand.
My American friend says she sleeps under a comforter. What is it?

A comforter, in American English, is a thick, soft bed cover filled with warm stuffing. It is a noun. It can also mean a person or thing that brings comfort.
Example: Isha pulled her comforter up to her chin on the cold night.
Who is a director in a film and in a company?

A director is a person who leads or manages something. In a film, the director decides how the story is shown. In a company, a director is a senior manager. It is a noun.
Example: The director asked the actors to repeat the scene.
What is glitter? We are using it for the craft day.

Glitter is tiny shiny pieces used for decoration. It is a noun. As a verb, glitter means to shine with small flashes of light.
Example: Priya sprinkled glitter on the card and shook off the extra.
Is reticent the same as shy?

Close, but not identical. Reticent means not eager to share your thoughts or feelings. A reticent person may be quiet for any reason, not only shyness. It is an adjective.
Example: He was reticent about his plans and only smiled when asked.
What are calculations? Our teacher says to show all of them in the exam.

Calculations are the steps of working out a number or answer with maths. It is a noun, in the plural here. Your teacher wants you to write the working, not only the final answer.
Example: Ravi did his calculations on the right side of the page and wrote the answer below.
My friend said the museum was fascinating. Does fascinating mean scary?

No. Fascinating means so interesting that it holds your attention strongly. It is an adjective. It has nothing to do with fear.
Example: The museum's display of old coins was fascinating, and we stayed for an hour.
I was named after my grandfather. Am I his namesake?

Yes. A namesake is a person or thing with the same name as another, especially one named after the other. It is a noun.
Example: Arun is his grandfather's namesake and shares his love of gardening.
It was so cold that my teeth began to chatter. Do teeth talk?

Not exactly. Here chatter is a verb meaning to knock together quickly and again and again, making a clicking sound, because of cold or fear. The other meaning is to talk fast about small things.
Example: The swimmers' teeth chattered as they climbed out of the cold lake.
The library charges a nominal fee for a card. I thought nominal was something to do with names.

Here nominal is an adjective meaning very small, so small that it is hardly more than a token amount. It comes from a word for name, so it can also mean existing in name only.
Example: The museum asks a nominal charge so that everyone can visit.
My uncle lives in staff quarters near the factory. Do quarters mean fourths of something?

Here quarters, in the plural, means a place where people live, especially provided by an employer or the army. It is a noun. The usual meaning is the four equal parts of a whole.
Example: The nurses live in quarters close to the hospital.
